text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGE triggered: realtime.p99 > SLO (us-west-2, route: /v1/generate). Alerting on-call.

sara: I’m on it. grabbing dashboards now — is customer-facing API affected or internal background jobs?

dmitri: p99 and p95 both spiked starting ~5299998800. Streaming routes show stalls; some clients report partial streams then timeout. cpu% high on a subset of inference hosts.

jen: Grafana: https://grafana.internal/r/abc123 (p99 overlay + topline request rate). looks like spike aligns with a deploy ~10m ago for model-quantization rollout.

ryan: possible model variant mismatch or kernel hot path. any autoscaler / quota noise?

ops-bot: Autoscaler attempted 6 scale-ups in last 12m; 4 failed due to quota limits on g4dn. Ticket filed but no automatic remediation.

sara: quick checks — running health + pod status

```
# from control plane
curl -sS https://realtime.us-west-2.internal/health | jq .
kubectl -n inference get pods -o wide --selector=route=realtime
kubectl -n inference logs pods/inference-xyz -c runtime | tail -n 80
```

dmitri: logs show repeated "kvcache miss" + heavy GC pauses on one node. sample:

```
2026-11-03T12:34:56Z runtime INFO kvcache miss key=ctx:abcd
2026-11-03T12:34:57Z runtime WARN GC pause 450ms
2026-11-03T12:35:02Z runtime ERROR tensor-copy timeout
```

jen: can we flip traffic to stable variant? route has rollout weight 70% new / 30% stable.

sara: yes — doing an immediate traffic shift to stable 100% for realtime route. will monitor p95/p99. executing now:

```
# deploy-runner
redwoodctl routes update realtime --variant stable --weight 100
```

sara: done. traffic now on stable variant. monitoring :eyes:

kb-bot: Automated check: model-stable has lower memory footprint; quantized rollout has known edge-case with larger contexts when prefix caching is disabled.

dmitri: after shift, p95 improved but p99 still elevated on streaming tail. looks like a subset of sessions stalled; possibly long-tail prefix rebuilds.

ryan: workaround idea — temporarily enable aggressive kv prefix caching and reduce max_batch_size to force faster dispatches.

sara: applying cache toggle and batch size change to route config. patch applied:

```
redwoodctl config set realtime kv_cache.enabled=true
redwoodctl config set realtime max_batch_size=8
```

jen: :thumbsup: I’ll watch traces. also checking if any infra nodes have oom/killed pods.

ops-bot: Note: reserved pool utilization is 98%, burst capacity enabled but limited by project quota. if this persists we should engage infra to increase quota or spin temporary instances in us-west-2.

sara: initial customer impact assessment: ~2.3% of realtime requests saw degraded streaming for ~12m window; top customers X,Y affected. Support page notified with EN queue.

ryan: can we enable fallback to lighter model for affected customers to preserve throughput? we have per-customer routing rules.

sara: rolling per-customer fallback for the top 3 affected customers now.

jen: p95 and p99 trending down after all mitigations. p99 still ~1.8x SLO for a tiny tail group.

dmitri: plan for next steps: (1) keep stable variant traffic until root cause (2) repro with quantization on staging (3) investigate GC and tensor-copy errors (4) request quota bump for burst pool.

sara: assigning follow-ups:
- dmitri: dig into runtime GC/tensor copy logs and identify node(s) to repro on (deadline +2h)
- eng-infra (ops-bot): open quota bump and temp capacity (ASAP)
- jen: validate end-to-end traces for stalled streaming sessions and gather sample session ids
- ryan: prepare rollback strategy for quantization rollout and a canary test plan

sara: notifying support & account teams for customers X,Y,Z. will post an incident summary in 60m. paging cleared but monitoring continues. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Incident assigned -> sara. Incident status: mitigated (live mitigation in place).
